title: Accel and Prosus Back Six Deep-Tech Startups in Inaugural India Cohort
excerpt: The venture firms selected six science-led companies from over 2,000 applications for their Atoms X LeapTech program, co-investing up to $2 million per startup.
body:
• Accel and Prosus have selected six startups spanning healthcare, climate, space, and longevity for their first joint Atoms X cohort in India.
  • The firms co-invest $500,000 to $2 million per startup, with Prosus matching Accel's capital, using a founder-friendly structure that defers some equity allocation.
  • Selected companies include Praan (air infrastructure), QOSMIC (satellite communications), EtherealX (reusable rockets), Dognosis (cancer detection from breath), Ferra (aging-focused strength training), and a stealth brain-computer interface startup.
  • The cohort was chosen from more than 2,000 applications, signaling growing depth in India's deep-tech ecosystem.

Accel and Prosus have picked six startups for their inaugural Atoms X LeapTech cohort in India, backing what the firms describe as "off-the-map" ideas in sectors where markets are undefined and development timelines stretch for years.

The joint program, announced in October 2025, focuses on science-led ventures that combine frontier research with engineering ambition. The six companies were selected from more than 2,000 applications across healthcare, climate infrastructure, space technology, and longevity.

The Selected Startups

The cohort spans a range of frontier technologies. Praan, based in Mumbai, is developing full-stack air infrastructure systems to improve indoor air quality through purification, sensing, and automated controls. QOSMIC, headquartered in Bengaluru, is building optical communication systems designed to increase bandwidth and reduce latency for data transfer between satellites and Earth.

Ethereal Exploration Guild, also known as EtherealX, is working on fully reusable orbital launch vehicles aimed at sharply reducing the cost of space access. The Bengaluru-based company previously raised a $20.5 million Series A round led by TDK Ventures and BIG Capital at an $80.5 million valuation.

Dognosis is developing technology to detect multiple cancers from breath samples, using dogs' olfactory capabilities along with robotics and AI. Its product, BreatheEasy, has patients breathe into a mask, with samples analyzed in a lab for cancer-linked biomarkers. Ferra is building a guided home-based strength training system that adjusts resistance automatically, targeting aging populations.

A sixth startup, operating in stealth mode, is developing brain-computer interface technology to enable direct communication between the brain and external systems.

Investment Structure

Under the partnership, Prosus matches Accel's capital commitment to each company, with individual investments ranging from $500,000 to $2 million. The firms have designed the investment structure to reduce early dilution for founders by deferring part of the equity allocation to a later stage.

"LeapTech requires conviction to build companies years before there is consensus. The quality of applications exceeded our expectations for Atoms X, showing how Indian founders around the world are building breakthroughs to commercialise science and create all-new categories."

— Pratik Agarwal, Partner at Accel

Ashutosh Sharma, head of India ecosystem at Prosus, said the response underscored a key gap in India's startup landscape. "Innovation in India is not constrained by ideas or inspiration. It is constrained by the right backing at the right time," he said, adding that Prosus aims to provide patient capital and global operating expertise to help founders "think in decades, not quarters."

India's Deep-Tech Shift

The program builds on Accel's broader Atoms initiative, launched in 2021 as a pre-seed scaling program. Atoms has since backed more than 50 startups that have collectively raised over $300 million in follow-on funding. Accel later expanded it to include two distinct tracks: Atoms AI, focused on artificial intelligence, and Atoms X, targeting what the firm calls LeapTech — innovations that go beyond conventional deep-tech.

The cohort reflects a broader shift in India's venture ecosystem toward frontier science bets. Indian startups in space, climate, and biotech have attracted increasing global attention as the country produces more engineers and researchers with the technical depth to build category-defining companies.

For the Indian diaspora, the program carries added significance. Several of the cohort's focus areas — space technology, healthcare diagnostics, and brain-computer interfaces — represent industries where Indian-origin researchers and entrepreneurs have long played leading roles globally. The Atoms X program creates a pathway for India-based founders to access the same caliber of patient capital and global networks.

Applications for future Atoms X cohorts are currently under evaluation, with the firms signaling an intent to expand the program as India's deep-tech pipeline matures.
